sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, accounting for roughly 38% of the model's importance.
Risk rises steeply once utilization passes about 0.74, and it rises across the full range of utilization from low to high values.
Past delinquencies are the second or third most important driver, and having any delinquency raises the predicted risk of default.
Annual income has a moderate to strong effect, and higher income is associated with lower predicted default risk.
Length of credit history has a weak to moderate effect, and longer histories generally lower the predicted risk.
The effect of utilization does not meaningfully depend on credit history length.
The data do not settle whether debt-to-income ratio matters for the model's predictions.
Feature_a, feature_b, applicant age and recent credit inquiries have at most a negligible effect on predicted default.
